narrative: OMX30 faces a low-conviction setup despite sitting +8.0% above the 200-MA. While ROC-90 momentum is strong at +5.5%, ADX weakness at 7.8 (well below 18) severely constrains trend reliability—applying the 30% confidence reduction per rules. NASDAQ's 0.77% decline weighs on tech sentiment, yet defensive positioning (gold +1.35%, VIX spiking) hints at tactical risk-off. Yields retreated 72bp and EUR/SEK weakened, creating mixed headwinds: stronger USD/SEK aids Volvo/Atlas Copco, but falling rates and oil (-0.90%) pressure industrials and real estate. RSI at 36.76 sits neutral but near oversold territory, flagging potential mean-reversion risk.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens with muted conviction. Weak ADX (7.8) strips confidence from the +8% bull case despite solid ROC-90 momentum. Watch 3123 (yesterday close) as pivot; support at 3085 (lower Bollinger), resistance 3180 (50-MA). NASDAQ weakness is a near-term headwind for Ericsson and Hexagon. However, gold's +1.35% rally supports Boliden, and USD/SEK strength (+0.34%) backs exporters Volvo/Atlas Copco. Oil's 0.90% drop weighs on Equinor-proxies and consumer spending appetite. Banks remain neutral—yield retreat offsets any NIM benefit. Key watch: US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET (labour market health) and Iran conflict escalation risk from news flow. Treat any intraday bounce as selling opportunity; lack of trend conviction argues for risk-off bias.
